transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling… wound up, I guess is the best way to put it. Almost all day, my body feels like it’s bracing for something, even when there’s nothing actually happening. Like I’ll be sitting at my computer trying to work, and I can feel this tension in me, like I’m on alert for some problem that hasn’t even shown up.

And it’s not just during work, either. Even after dinner, when I’m supposed to be relaxing, I still feel kind of keyed up, like I can’t fully settle. It’s uncomfortable, and it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should finally come talk to someone about it.
Do you find yourself worrying about a variety of things, like work, family, health, or other everyday concerns, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

Yes… yes, I do. It’s like my mind doesn’t stay on one thing for very long, it just keeps moving from one concern to the next. I’ll think about my sister in Arecibo and whether everything is okay with her, and then almost immediately I’m thinking about work, like maybe I missed an email or forgot to do something important at the office.

And then it jumps again—my husband driving home, whether he’s safe, whether traffic is bad, things like that. Or I’ll start thinking about church commitments, whether I said I’d help with something and didn’t write it down, or whether I’m falling behind on bills even when there isn’t necessarily a problem right in front of me.

It’s not always one big dramatic worry. It’s more like I’m constantly preparing for something to go wrong before anything has even happened. I catch myself making little plans in my head for problems that don’t actually exist yet.
Do you feel like you’re able to control these worries, or do they feel overwhelming and difficult to manage most of the time?

They’re difficult to control, yes. I mean, I try—I really do try to stop myself. I’ll be sitting there and I’ll literally say in my head, Daniela, enough, focus on this report, just finish the thing in front of you. And for maybe a minute I can do that, but then one small thought comes in, like, did I answer that message, or what if I forgot something important, and then it turns into five more thoughts.

Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or going back over things in my mind, replaying what could go wrong. And it’s frustrating because part of me knows I’m not solving anything by doing that, but it feels hard to let it go once it starts. Like my mind keeps pulling me back to it even when I’m trying to move on.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms along with these worries, like restlessness, muscle tension, or feeling easily fatigued?

Yes, definitely the wound-up feeling. That’s probably the clearest physical part of it for me. It’s like my body is tense before I’ve even figured out what I’m worried about, if that makes sense.

I can be sitting at my computer, just doing ordinary work, and I notice I’m sort of braced—like I’m waiting for something to go wrong. Not panicking exactly, but not relaxed either. And then even later, after dinner, when nothing is really being asked of me, I still don’t fully settle down. I’ll be sitting there and my body still feels on alert, like I should be preparing for something.

It’s uncomfortable because I know, logically, nothing is happening in that moment, but physically I feel wound up almost all day.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because your mind is racing or you feel too tense to relax?

Yes… sleep is not terrible every single night, but it’s not restful the way it used to be. Most nights I do fall asleep eventually, after turning things over in my head for a while, but then I’ll wake up around three or four in the morning and my mind just sort of starts up again.

It’ll be something like my sister’s next appointment—whether she has a ride, whether I should call her, whether I forgot to ask something—or it’ll be work, like some server issue or whether something is going to break and I’ll have missed the warning signs. And once that thought is there, it’s hard to just roll over and go back to sleep. I’ll lie there trying to tell myself, “There’s nothing you can do about this at three in the morning,” but my body doesn’t really believe me.

So even if, technically, I’ve been in bed long enough and maybe got enough hours altogether, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest. Like I slept, but I didn’t recover, if that makes sense.
Do you ever feel this way even when things are going well or there isn't any specific stressor happening in your life?

Yes, I do. That’s actually one of the things that bothers me most, because it doesn’t always match what’s happening around me.

Even when nothing is immediately wrong, my mind will start moving from one thing to another. I’ll think about my sister in Arecibo and whether she’s okay, and then somehow that turns into whether I forgot something at the office, or if there’s some issue I missed that’s going to become a bigger problem later. Then I’ll think about my husband driving home, like whether he’s gotten there safely, and then church commitments, bills, little things I need to follow up on… it just keeps going.

And it’s not always that there’s a real crisis. A lot of the time I’m preparing in my head for problems that haven’t even happened. Like I’m trying to get ahead of something, but I don’t even know what the “something” is yet. So yes, even when things are basically fine, I can still feel like my mind is looking for the next thing to worry about.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, like your heart racing, shortness of breath, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?

I don’t think so… not in that sudden, out-of-nowhere way you’re describing.

I mean, I do get very uncomfortable and keyed up, and sometimes I can feel like something is going to go wrong, but it’s more of a drawn-out, simmering thing than a big wave that hits all at once. I don’t usually have a moment where I suddenly think, “Oh no, I can’t breathe,” or feel like I’m about to collapse or anything like that.

It’s more that I’m already tense and my mind keeps circling around possibilities. So if my heart is beating a little faster or I feel unsettled, it feels connected to all that worrying rather than like a separate episode that comes on quickly. At least, that’s how it seems to me.
Have you ever felt this way even when nothing particularly stressful or upsetting was happening in your life?

Yes, and that’s part of what feels so frustrating. It’s not always because something big is happening. Sometimes things are basically fine, or at least nothing new has gone wrong, and my mind still starts moving.

It’ll go from one thing to the next—my sister in Arecibo, whether she’s okay or needs something, then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I missed something at the office, or whether there’s some problem I should have caught. Then I’ll think about my husband driving home and whether he got there safely, and then it’s church commitments, bills, errands, messages I need to return… it’s like my brain is scanning for something to worry about.

And a lot of it is me trying to prepare for problems that haven’t even happened. I’ll be thinking, “Well, what if this comes up?” or “What if I forgot that?” even when there isn’t actually a real issue in front of me. It’s like I can’t just accept that things are okay for the moment.
